messages:
alex: Quick sketch: we need a lightweight compat layer so Python/TS/Go SDKs can opt into the same retry + pagination semantics without leaking transport details. thinking: a small iterator + policy object per call.

sarah: +1. want to avoid making resume tokens transport-specific. Consumers shouldn't have to know HTTP vs gRPC.

mike: Agree. Two options: (A) opaque resume token (blob) + SDK handles decode and rehydrate transport state, or (B) explicit session object that can be passed between calls and adapters implement it.

priya: pros/cons: opaque token -> easiest for server-side changes, but makes debugging hard. explicit session -> clearer for SDK users (can inspect) but couples surface to language bindings.

alex: Good summary. Another constraint: cloud routes can fallback across model variants and regions. tokens need to be stable across fallbacks.

mike: For retries, we also need to support idempotency hints (user-visible) vs internal retry. i propose a Policy struct with fields: max_retries, backoff_strategy, idempotency_hint. SDKs map that to transport semantics.

priya: Implementation note: keep runtime-side state minimal. For streaming endpoints we can store a small KV of last-offset + checksum. Example resume token payload we discussed:
```json
{"v":1,"off":1024,"ck":"a3f2", "sess":"e3b.."}
```
But encode as base64 to keep opaque.

alex: If we use base64 opaque token, add a short prefix for version+type so older clients can refuse rather than misinterpret. e.g. `r1:` then base64.

sarah: Question: should SDKs expose any of the retry budget/batch hints? customers asked for backpressure controls. Maybe expose read-only telemetry on remaining budget.

mike: We can add a ReadOnly Session.getBudget() on the explicit session approach. But again that leaks runtime to user. Perhaps add an admin/telemetry API on Console instead.

priya: For language ergonomics: TS wants async iterators, Python wants async generator + sync fallback, Go wants channel-style iterator. The compat layer should be an abstract "Pager" interface and adapters that convert to idiomatic constructs.

alex: Agreed. So final proposal:
- Keep resume token opaque (base64 blob with v+type prefix) so server can change internals.
- SDKs provide a high-level Pager abstraction; adapters convert to async iterator / generator / channel.
- Policy object for retries/backoff/idempotency that maps to transport specifics.
- Optional Session object for advanced users that can expose read-only telemetry (budget, last-offset) but not mutate internals.

sarah: My concern: debugging opaqueness. We should include an optional human-readable debug string in token metadata (not required to parse). that helps support.

mike: +1 to debug field. Also we need a migration plan for token version bumps. server returns specific error code if token unsupported; SDKs should surface a clear error message with link to docs.

priya: I'll draft an RFC with example Pager API signatures for each lang and a token layout. Will include sample code for converting token->session in case teams want advanced control.

alex: Thanks — prioritize backwards compatibility story and simple defaults. @ci-bot run quick matrix tests on py/ts/go iterators once the RFC lands? :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Scheduled job 'iterator-compat-matrix' queued — will run on PR merge.

alex: cool, will post RFC link here when ready.
